svg.title: The stdio transport and the Streamable HTTP transport, side by side
svg.desc: Two panels of equal size. On the left, stdio: a host box sits above the server process with three pipes between them, standard input carrying requests down, and standard output and standard error carrying frames and logs back up. Beneath it, two newline-terminated JSON objects, and notes that there is one JSON object per line and no port, URL or certificate. On the right, Streamable HTTP: the same host box POSTs to a single endpoint, with the request line and the protocol and method headers shown, and the server answers either 200 OK application slash json or 200 OK text slash event-stream. Notes say the reply is one object or a stream scoped to that request, and that there is no session header so any replica may answer. A closing line says neither transport is the advanced one and the choice follows from who is allowed to run the process.
svg.text: One message format, two ways for the bytes to travel
Same JSON-RPC, same _meta. Only the framing and the metadata carrier differ.
The host spawns your program as a child process.
One JSON object per line. Nothing else, ever.
No port, no URL, no certificate.
Your program listens. Any client may POST to it.
One object, or a stream scoped to this request.
No session header. Any replica may answer.
Neither is the advanced one. Choose by who is allowed to run the process.
